report.summary: Error rate on api-gateway jumped from ~0.4% to ~14% at the 17:00 bucket, right after two changes logged at 16:57:00Z: an auth-service v4.0.0 deploy (new v2 session token format, v1 still accepted) and a netops gateway rate-limit change tightening /api/* burst from 200 to 20 per client. The gateway rate-limit change is the best fit for the 'too many requests' errors, since the 20x tighter burst lines up with the onset. Auth-service traffic rose from ~80 to ~107 req/s at the same time, with token-refresh warnings for expired or invalid sessions, which fits the sign-outs and may be a retry or refresh amplification effect. Gateway logs were inaccessible, so the 429 attribution is unverified. Health checks are all green, so they do not detect this degradation.

root_cause.mechanism: The netops rate-limit change cut the /api/* per-client burst from 200 to 20, so normal client bursts are rejected with 429 'too many requests'. Rejected clients retry and fail to refresh sessions, which generates the sign-out reports and the auth refresh traffic increase.
assumptions: The change was in effect at 17:00.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The netops rate-limit change cut the /api/* per-client burst from 200 to 20, so normal client bursts are rejected with 429 'too many requests'. Rejected clients retry and fail to refresh sessions, which generates the sign-out reports and the auth refresh traffic increase.
assumptions: The change was in effect at 17:00.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v4.0.0 deploy changed session token issuance to v2. Clients or validators that mishandle v2 tokens see them as expired or invalid, which forces sign-outs and refresh loops that raise auth request volume.
assumptions: Token refresh failures are caused by v2 token handling.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: A client-side traffic surge or retry storm hit the gateway's /api/* routes and triggered rate limiting.
assumptions: The auth surge reflects client traffic.

observed_facts.statement: api-gateway error_rate was 0.36–0.45% from 16:00 to 16:55, then 14.83% at 17:00 and 13.6–14.6% through 17:30.
Two changes were recorded at 16:57:00Z: auth-service deploy v4.0.0 (session tokens issued in v2 format, v1 still accepted) and api-gateway config change lowering /api/* burst 200 -> 20 per client.
auth-service request_rate rose from 82.39 req/s (16:55) to 108.05 req/s (17:00), staying ~104–108 through 17:30; it was 77.8–81 req/s before.

auth-service logged repeated 'token refresh requested for expired or invalid session' WARNs from 17:00:32 onward (10 in the window), plus one 'rejected malformed Authorization header' ERROR at 17:01:01.
auth-service CPU (~25%), memory (~43–46%), p99 latency (~40 ms) and error rate (~0.1%) stayed flat across 17:00.
api-gateway latency p99 stayed ~175–187 ms and CPU ~38% across the window, with no change at 17:00.
All health checks (api-gateway, auth-service, checkout-service, search-service) returned HTTP 200 at 17:28.

assumptions: The 4xx responses are 429 rate-limit rejections produced by the new burst=20 policy (not verified; gateway logs are inaccessible).
The health checks are shallow and do not exercise rate limiting or token validation of v2 tokens.
The 16:57 timestamps for the two changes are accurate and both took effect before the 17:00 bucket.
Users were signed out because clients failed token refresh or v2 token handling, not because of a password or credential change.
(unverified - no valid evidence cited) api-gateway WARN/ERROR log query failed with 'access denied: requires elevated permissions'.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The gateway rate-limit policy change (burst 200->20) most likely explains the 14% 4xx spike and the 'too many requests' errors, since it coincides with the onset and the request rate did not change at the gateway (~422 req/s, flat).

The auth-service v4.0.0 deploy is a plausible contributor to sign-outs, via token format incompatibility or refresh loops that double auth traffic, but auth error rate and latency did not rise, which weakens a hard-failure explanation.
The gateway request rate was unchanged while auth traffic rose ~30%, so the auth surge is probably client-side retries after the 429s or sign-outs, not an independent traffic surge.

remediation.action: Roll back the api-gateway rate-limit change (burst 20 -> 200) to restore /api/* access.
remediation.rationale: The change is the best-supported cause and the rollback is low-risk and fast.

remediation.action: Pause or roll back auth-service v4.0.0 pending verification of v2 token handling, if sign-outs persist after the gateway rollback.
remediation.rationale: The deploy is coincident with the sign-outs and refresh warnings; its impact is not yet confirmed.

remediation.action: Obtain gateway log access to confirm the 4xx status codes are 429 and identify the affected clients and routes.
remediation.rationale: Current attribution rests on timing alone.

remediation.action: Add a canary or staged rollout for rate-limit changes and a 4xx-by-status alert.
remediation.rationale: The change went straight to production with no alert on rejections.

remediation.action: Add deep health checks covering token validation and rate-limit behaviour.
remediation.rationale: The health checks were green during a user-facing outage.

open_questions: What are the 4xx status codes at the gateway (429 vs 401 vs 403), and which routes do they hit?
Did the v4.0.0 auth deploy cause token validation failures, or is the sign-out purely client-side refresh behaviour?
Why did the auth request rate rise ~30% at 17:00 with no gateway traffic change?
Is the 16:57 timestamp for both changes exact, and which took effect first?
